chapter: New Orleans clubs and Sharky's band
title: The Spotlight Bar and Snoozer Quinn
summary: First piano player at the Spotlight Bar; guitarist Snoozer Quinn sat in with him.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, you knew a lot of the controversy that went on with him with the police department, and he was one of the finest men that I ever met in my life, and one of my best friends. And he used to come in and sit down and drink while I was playing all the time. And one of the first jobs I had also was at the, I was the first piano player they ever had in the spotlight bar, which is where the Royal Sinesta is now. The spotlight was right across the street from the famous door.
That was where Snoozer Quinn used to come there and set in with me.
Snoozer Quinn was one of the finest guitar players in the world.
Have you ever heard this boy that Lloyd Ellis that plays with Pete? I have heard of him. And he plays with Jimmy Ile?

Snoozer and Lloyd Ellis played very, very much alike. And Snoozer and I were good friends and we only met. He said one, he came in there one night, he says, I sure like the way you play. He says, I play a little guitar. He said, would you mind if I played a little bit with you? I said, no, sir, I'd be tickled to death. Boy, when he took that guitar out of that case and started to, there was no amplification. Just the guitar by itself. But it had a tone out of this world. And how he played was nobody's business. And I had heard of him and I didn't know his name at the time. I said, well, what is your name? He says, Snoozer Quinn. I nearly fell off the piano stool to have such an honor because I was just getting started. Don't you see?
Yeah, I think I've heard people talk about him at the firm.
Oh, I've got his picture in that Hall of Fame. You know, the Family Album, you know, the Doc Sushant. I've got all of those things.
